newsitem.title: UK: UK Labour to clamp down on drug crime, guns.
newsitem.headline: UK Labour to clamp down on drug crime, guns.

text.p: Labour, claiming to be Britain's only party of law and order, promised on Thursday to ban private ownership of handguns and crack down on drug-related crime if it wins the coming general election.

In a speech to the main opposition party's annual conference, home affairs spokesman Jack Straw said Britain's streets risked becoming as mean as America's unless Labour tackled crime and the inequalities that spawned it.
"We can't go on like this," said Straw, whose party has been taking a harder line on law and order to outflank the ruling Conservatives in the run-up to the election, due by May.
"If you want a picture of what it could be like, of what happens if you don't get tough on crime and tough on the causes of crime, then look across the Atlantic.

"Look to see the wealthy barricade themselves in suburban fortresses, the poor trapped in ghettoes, millions owning guns for their self-defence, and a prison population which has tripled in two decades," Straw said.

He said a Labour government would make sweeping changes to Britain's gun laws to avert a repeat of the Dunblane tragedy in March, when a lone gunman killed 16 children and their teacher in a Scottish primary school before shooting himself dead.

Labour, in opposition since 1979, would ban the private ownership and possession of all handguns, end mail order sales, ban all under-18s from holding airguns and shotguns, and introduce a stricter gun licensing system.
"We cannot have a society which values the right of civilians to own a handgun more than that of a child to a future," Straw said to loud applause.
To break the link between drugs and crime, he pledged to make addicts undergo treatment and random drug tests.

Straw said: "With heroin addicts thieving daily to fund their habit, at a cost of well over one billion pounds ($1.5 billion) in property stolen each year, it is time call a halt to this vicious circle of addiction and crime."
Straw condemned the ruling Conservatives for presiding over a doubling of crime during their 17 years in office and said today a crime would be committed in Britain every two seconds.
Labour would make sentencing more consistent, ensure fast-track justice for persistent young offenders and crack down on noisy and disruptive neighbours.
"There is now only one party of law and order, and that party is the Labour Party," he said.
